title: Special Order for Louisiana Public Service Commission, ex parte. — This Special Order ratifies votes taken by Commissioner Francis acting as the Commission’s representative on the Board of Directors of the Organization of MISO States.

documents.text:
LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                             SPECIAL ORDER NUMBER 72-2026

                       LOUISIANA PUBLIC SERVICE COMMISSION
                                    EX PARTE

In re: This Special Order ratifies votes taken by Commissioner Francis acting as the
Commission’s representative on the Board of Directors of the Organization of MISO States.

                (Decided at the October 22, 2026 Business and Executive Session.)


                                              ORDER

I.      OVERVIEW

        This matter was on the agenda for ratification of votes taken on September 10, 11, 18, and
October 5, 2026 by Commissioner Francis as the LPSC’s representative on the Organization of
MISO States ("OMS") Board of Directors. Staff followed the protocols set forth in Special Order
17-2019 to consult with the Executive Secretary and Chairman and to make a recommendation to
Commissioner Francis prior to the vote. The protocols also require that any votes taken be ratified
at a following B&E. The vote to be ratified is summarized as follows:

     1. At its September 10, 2026 board meeting, the OMS approved a position statement on
        Auction Revenue Rights (ARR) and Financial Transmission Rights (FTR) enhancements.
        The OMS Position Statement supported a proposal to allocate ARR entitlements seasonally
        and increase transmission outage reporting. These changes are intended to benefit
        ratepayers. On Staff recommendation, the LPSC voted in favor of the OMS pleading.

     2. The OMS conducted an email vote on September 11, 2026 on comments for filing in FERC
        Docket ER26-3552, a MISO application related to its Zero Injection Generator
        Interconnection Agreement (ZGIA) proposal. The MISO ZGIA proposal is intended to
        provide a path for large loads to quickly interconnect to the grid through an arrangement
        where the large load is being served by generation that is in close with an agreement that
        the load will not draw from the grid and that the generation will not inject into the grid.The
        OMS comments conditionally support MISO’s ZGIA framework as a potential tool for
        addressing the need for quicker interconnection of large loads with the caveat that MISO’s
        ZGIA framework should be implemented only with appropriate safeguards to ensure that
        expedited interconnection does not create increased reliability risks, provide preferential
        treatment, or shift costs to existing customers. Based on Staff’s recommendation, the LPSC
        voted in favor of the OMS Comments.

     3. The OMS conducted an email vote on 9/18/26 on comments for filing in FERC Docket
        ER26-3650, a MISO application related to its compliance with the FERC show cause
        directive related to interconnection reliability and data transparency issues associated with
        the interconnection of large loads. The OMS comments generally support the MISO filing,
        which creates rules applicable to loads 50 MW or greater. It creates requirements related
        to data visibility, Phasor Measurement Units (PMU), Ramp and Ride-Through intended to
        comply with FERC requirements. Based on Staff’s recommendation, the LPSC voted in
        favor of the OMS Comments.

     4. The OMS conducted a vote at its October 5, 2026 special board meeting on comments to
        be filed in FERC Docket No. ER26-3813, a MISO proceeding designed to speed up its
        normal generator interconnection queue process, including its 2022 process, by providing
        a one-time, unconditional opportunity to withdraw from the queue penalty-free at Decision
        Point II. This provision, if approved, would encourage the timely exit for unviable projects
        and, thereby, accelerate the study process for later DPP cycles. Based on Staff’s
        recommendation, the LPSC voted in favor of the OMS Comments.

                                                                         Special Order No. 72-2026
                                                                                            Page 1
 II.    COMMISSION JURISDICTION AND AUTHORITY

       The jurisdiction of the Commission is set forth by the Louisiana Constitution Article IV,
Section 21, which provides:

              The commission shall regulate all common carriers and public
              utilities and have such other regulatory authority as provided by law.
              It shall adopt and enforce reasonable rules, regulations, and
              procedures necessary for the discharge of its duties, and shall have
              other powers and perform other duties as provided by law.


III.   CONCLUSION

       This matter was placed on the Commission’s October 22, 2026 B&E Agenda for
ratification by the full Commission. On motion of Chairman Skrmetta, seconded by Vice
Chairman Coussan, with Commissioner Campbell and Commissioner Lewis concurring, and
Commissioner Francis abstaining, the Commission voted to ratify the votes cast by Commissioner
Francis on September 10, 11, 18, and October 5, 2026 as the Louisiana Public Service Commission
representative to the OMS Board of Directors.


This Order is effective immediately.


BY ORDER OF THE COMMISSION
BATON ROUGE, LOUISIANA
November 17, 2026
